newsitem.title: GERMANY: ProSieben sees room for share price gains.
newsitem.headline: ProSieben sees room for share price gains.

text.p: German television group ProSieben Media AG said on Monday that the price range of its initial public offering of 66-72 marks ($41.66) still left room for share price gains when the stock begins trading on July 7.

ProSieben Chairman Georg Kofler, speaking at a news conference, dismissed criticism that the IPO range was too high. He said that based on the company's price-earnings-ratio, forecast to be around 18 next year, which he said was lower than the market average.
"If we remain below the market average, then it will be shown that we were relatively humble and there will be a little potential for price gains," he said.

The bookbuilding period to subscribe to the ProSieben issue begins on Tuesday and ends on July 3. The offer price will be announced on July 5 at 1730 GMT during the ProSieben nightly news broadcast. Shares begin trading on July 7.
ProSieben chief finance officer Lothar Lanz said he expected around half of the 17.5 million non-voting preference shares will be placed in Germany and the rest with international investors.
The company is also seeking a private placement 144a in the United States.
Asked about the dividend, Kofler and Lanz would not comment on market forecasts, only saying that the dividend will be "oriented towards earnings".
Analysts have forecast a dividend for 1997 of around 40 pfennigs and for 1998 of 1.50 marks.
